title: Pen Test Communications, Evidence Retention, and Remediation Guidelines
content:
Purpose:
This document defines a repeatable, low-friction pattern for coordinating third-party and internal penetration tests against Redwood Inference infrastructure. It focuses on how we communicate with stakeholders, what evidence we collect and retain, how we export and verify SIEM ingests, and a pragmatic remediation plan template that ties findings back to RBAC, audit logging, and SIEM mapping requirements.

Intended audience:
- Security engineers running assessments
- Engineering owners for scoped services (serving-runtime, platform-engineering, private-deployments)
- SRE and observability teams
- Product and legal stakeholders for contract-level scoping and evidence retention

Scope of this guide:
- Pre-engagement communications and kickoff checklist
- Evidence definition and retention mapping for audit logs and telemetry (what fields we must capture)
- SIEM export verification checklist and common transformation pitfalls
- Evidence automation hooks and sample extraction queries
- Findings summary template and prioritized remediation plan tied to RBAC and audit schema gaps

1) Pre-engagement checklist (to be completed 2 weeks before test)
- Confirm statement of work (SOW) and allowed test window. Attach copy to Jira ticket and link to Confluence (SOW id).
- Identify service and environment scope (hosted-api, dedicated clusters, private VPCs). Explicitly list IP ranges and credentials allowed for testing.
- Approve proof-of-concept actions (e.g., exploitation of low-risk N-day vs. destructive actions). Approval must be documented by legal and product.
- RACI for the engagement:
  - Requester (Security Eng): coordinate vendor and internal ops.
  - Owners (Service SMEs): observed service, own mitigation.
  - SRE/Observability: ensure logs and retention windows meet evidence needs.
  - Privacy/Legal: contract and PII risk.
- Evidence escrow: define where evidence will live (S3 bucket with restricted access, ticketing attachments, and mirror in SIEM).
- Backup and rollback: confirm hourly snapshots for stateful systems where tests may run intrusive checks.

2) Evidence and audit-log retention mapping (minimum required fields)
We consider two evidence buckets: (A) Authentication and access control events and (B) Model/Inference access and configuration events. For each event type, the minimum required schema fields are listed. These are non-negotiable for a pen-test evidence package.

A. Authentication and access control events (examples: user-login, token-issue, oauth-refresh, session-terminate, rbac-grant, rbac-revoke)
- timestamp (ISO-8601)
- event_id (UUID)
- principal_id (user/email/service-account)
- principal_type (human/service-token/automation)
- action (login, token_create, token_revoke, rbac_change)
- outcome (success/failure)
- source_ip
- user_agent
- request_id (trace id)
- target_resource (resource id or ARNs)
- changed_fields (for config changes; free-text)
- request_payload_hash (sha256) or request_summary
- retention_tag (e.g., pen-test-2025-10)

B. Model and inference access events (examples: model-load, model-invoke, kvcache-evict, policy-eval)
- timestamp
- event_id
- requester_id
- model_id (catalog id and pinned version)
- model_variant (quantized/int8/float16)
- endpoint_id
- input_size_tokens
- output_size_tokens
- latency_ms
- request_route (API path)
- response_status (200/4xx/5xx)
- policy_decision (allowed/denied/fallback)
- cached_hit (true/false)
- trace_id

Retention policy: For pen-tests we require a minimum 90-day retention for objects and 180-day retention for authentication events that may be used in forensic timelines. Archive copies should be immutable (WORM) for the duration of the engagement plus 90 days.

3) SIEM export and verification checklist
- Confirm ingestion pipeline includes raw event fields (do not drop request_payload_hash or trace_id).
- Validate timestamp normalization across sources (UTC, ISO-8601). Check for clock skew > 2s across key hosts.
- Verify mapping logic for principal_type and outcome codes.
- Ensure RBAC change events are indexed with changed_fields and prior_state fields (if available).
- Test search queries: a) failed login spikes last 24h b) RBAC grant events for high-priv roles last 7d c) model-invoke events from unexpected IPs last 30d.
- Verify retention and access control on SIEM side (who can export evidence).

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Transformed logs lose request_id: add a transformation audit step that preserves original request_id to raw_message.
- Redaction removes too much context: maintain a redaction map that keeps identifiers needed for correlation (trace_id, event_id).
- SIEM field name collisions: use namespaced field prefixes (ri_auth_*, ri_model_*).

4) Evidence automation hooks (how we generate the package)
We recommend a tiny automation pipeline that produces a forensics bundle and sanity checks. Minimal components:
- extraction script (python) that pulls events from logstore/BigQuery/Elasticsearch for event ranges matching the test window and exports NDJSON to S3 with a manifest.json.
- verification script that runs signature checks (sha256) across each file, cross-checks counts against SIEM ingestion counts, and validates required fields are present.
- packaging: signed tarball with a simple index.csv and a timeline.csv for quick review.

Example extraction query (pseudo-ES DSL):
  index: ri-audit-*
  time_range: 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z TO 2025-10-03T23:59:59Z
  must: [term: {retention_tag: "pen-test-2025-10"}], [exists: {field: "trace_id"}]

Verification checks (exit non-zero on failure):
- manifest.count == total_lines_in_ndjson
- every event has timestamp and event_id
- no PII exposures outside encrypted archive (scans for email patterns in plaintext fields)

5) Findings summary template (one-page per finding)
- Finding ID: SEC-PT-YYYY-NNN
- Title: short, imperative phrase (e.g., Incomplete RBAC enforcement on /admin/config)
- Affected scope: services, endpoints, cluster ids, regions
- Evidence snapshot: timestamps and event_ids collected, SIEM query references, S3 object keys
- Technical impact: concise explanation and exploitability level
- Business impact: what customer/data could be affected
- Severity (High/Medium/Low) and justification
- Recommended immediate mitigations (short-term)
- Recommended long-term remediation with owner and ETA
- Verification steps (how to prove fixed)

6) Prioritization matrix for remediation (simple scoring)
- Score = (Exploitability 1-5) + (Impact 1-5) + (Detectability modifier -1..+1)
- Triage buckets: P0 (>=12) immediate mitigation, P1 9-11 address within 2 weeks, P2 6-8 roadmap, P3 <=5 low risk

7) Sample remediation playbooks (RBAC / Audit gaps / SIEM)
Scenario A: RBAC grant endpoints not audited
- Short-term: add a logging wrapper around grant APIs to emit a ri_auth_rbac_change event with prior_state and new_state; enable retention_tag for pen-test. Owner: platform-engineering. SLA: 48 hours.
- Long-term: enforce RBAC change through centralized policy service with immutable audit records (append-only). Add alert in SIEM for unindexed RBAC events. Owner: eng-platform. ETA: 3 sprints.

Scenario B: Missing trace_id in transformed SIEM logs
- Short-term: change log forwarder to include original trace_id in raw_message and add ri_meta_trace_id. Owner: observability. SLA: 24 hours.
- Long-term: update transformation pipeline to preserve and rename fields with ri_ prefix; add test in CI that validates trace_id persists. Owner: observability. ETA: 2 sprints.

Scenario C: Model-invoke events show no model_variant or latency
- Short-term: instrument inference runtime to emit ri_model_invoke with model_id and latency_ms; set sampling to 100% for test window. Owner: serving-runtime. SLA: 72 hours.
- Long-term: bake instrumentation into runtime release and include in release checklist. Owner: serving-runtime. ETA: next minor version.

8) Communication templates and timelines
- Initial kickoff email (to vendor + owners): short template with SOW, allowed IPs, test window, escalation contacts, evidence location, and expected retention.
- Daily status update template (during test): summary of top findings, SIEM anomalies, evidence uploads with S3 keys.
- Post-engagement package delivery: list of artifacts (tarball, manifest, timeline.csv), verification report, and final action items grouped by owner.

9) Verification and closeout checklist
- Sanity check: every finding in vendor report has evidence_id linking to our package.
- For High/Medium findings: ensure an owner is assigned and remediation ETA is in Jira; a verification ticket is created with test steps.
- Archive the evidence bundle to immutable storage and log the archive_id in the closeout ticket.
- If PII was exposed, notify Privacy and Legal and follow incident disclosure workflow.

Appendix A: Quick reference SIEM queries
- Failed logins in last 24h:
  ri_auth_event.outcome:failure AND @timestamp:[now-24h TO now]
- RBAC grants to high-priv role in last 7d:
  ri_auth_rbac_change.changed_fields:role AND ri_auth_rbac_change.new_state:*("admin" OR "operator")
- Model invokes from external IPs last 30d:
  ri_model_invoke AND NOT ri_model_invoke.request_route: "/internal/*" AND source_ip:[!10.0.0.0/8]

Appendix B: Minimal acceptance criteria for evidence bundle
- Contains NDJSON of raw events and a signed manifest
- All files SHA256-signed and signature included in manifest
- Timeline.csv with ordered event_id,timestamp,principal,short-summary
- Verification report (JSON or markdown) with checks run and pass/fail

Notes and open questions (to resolve before next test):
- Should retention defaults for internal audit logs be extended to 365 days for high-risk services? (security/product)
- Define exact RBAC role names that trigger high-priority alerts in SIEM (platform-engineering/security)
- Add CI check to prevent transformation pipelines from dropping trace_id (observability)

End of document.
